data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient than a single large service because the large service's internal redundancy is subject to a shared administrative and operational sphere that acts as a single point of failure for failure-mode diversity.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the decentralized operators all outsource their administration to the same third-party (e.g., the same cloud provider), the administrative shared cause reappears.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the large service can maintain strictly siloed administrative teams with zero shared dependencies, the mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Even if a large service has logically isolated sub-services, they share a common administrative backbone (e.g., one HR department, one security policy, one deployment pipeline). A failure in this shared administrative layer (e.g., a bad security patch pushed to all internal sub-services) can simultaneously compromise all internal redundancy. The decentralized network, lacking this shared administrative backbone, is immune to this specific class of correlated failure. The shared cause is not technical but organizational.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
